mcq.q: A site crashes every sale day because everything runs on one database. Restarting the server only addresses which iceberg level?

written.q: Explain systems thinking using the iceberg model and give a software example.
written.a: Systems thinking looks beyond surface fixes to the network of causes and effects. Iceberg levels: events (what happened), patterns (what is happening over time), structures (what enables the pattern), mental models (beliefs that sustain the structures). Example: a site crashes (event) every sale (pattern) because there is one database and no cache (structure), due to the belief that traffic will stay small (mental model). Fix the structure and the belief, not just restart the server.

written.q: List and explain five design-thinking mindsets.
written.a: Driven by curiosity (ask WH questions, change perspective); focus on the people (empathy, human needs); accept complexity (uncertainty, complex problems need complex solutions); experiment and iterate (prototype and test with users); networked collaboration (agile, ad hoc work with T-shaped people and U-shaped teams). Others: visualise and show, co-create grow and scale, varying mental states, process awareness, reflect on actions.

written.q: Describe divergent and convergent thinking, the groan zone and the double-diamond process.
written.a: Divergent thinking opens up options and perspectives; convergent thinking prioritises, selects and refines. The groan zone is the uncomfortable middle that needs facilitation before the point of decision. Double diamond: think like a system (Discover: behaviour-led research; Define: workshops and idea generation, producing the problem definition) then act like an entrepreneur (Develop: review ideas; Deliver: prototyping, selection, mentoring).
